item.title: Intergroup Connectivity and Religious Resilience: An Agent-Based Model of an Orthodox Religious Community
item.description: Empty

item.title: Stability, Silence, Community, and Psychotherapy: What Young People Are Looking for in Religion
item.description: English translation of a Forbes Young article by Elena Strelkova. On Gen Z religiosity in Russia and globally, featuring expert commentary.

item.title: What Does the Modern Person Believe? From Horoscopes to Neural Networks
item.description: Lecture transcript, Moscow, May 2026. On the contemporary religious situation, secularization theory, and the transformation of religion.

item.title: Parody Religions: From Discordia to the Flying Spaghetti Monster
item.description: Lecture transcript, Moscow, March 2026. On the sociology of parody religiosity — from Pastafarianism to Discordianism and the Church of the SubGenius.

item.title: Does a Secular Course in Religious Studies Affect Religiosity? A Proposed Randomised Experiment
item.description:
Does a Secular Course in Religious Studies Affect Religiosity? A Proposed Randomised Experiment

Essay for the course “Introduction to Causality” Nikita Obraztsov, European University at St. Petersburg, 2025

item.title: The Concept of Belonging Without Believing in the Context of Orthodox Identity Formation in Russia
item.description: Conference paper presented at the VII All-Russian Sociological Congress, Moscow, November 2025. On the gap between declared Orthodox affiliation and actual religious practice in contemporary Russia.

item.title: What Does It Mean to Be a Rational Person?
item.description: Based on an appearance on the Pascal's Wager podcast. On the nature of rationality, its limits, astrology, and why rationality is a tool rather than a sacred cow.

item.title: Does Religion Exist? Three Approaches to Studying It
item.description: Realism, phenomenology, and constructivism — three frameworks scholars use when approaching the phenomenon of religion. A breakdown with examples and criticism of each.

item.title: Feynman on Science, Religion, and Doubt
item.description: A reading of The Meaning of It All. Why scientists tend not to believe, what NOMA gets right, and where Feynman goes wrong on religion.

item.title: Machiavelli on Religion: Analyses of his views
item.description: What Machiavelli thought about religion, why he almost never used the word God, how his views differed from Luther's, and whether he belongs among the freethinkers.

item.title: Religious Meanings in the Harry Potter Novels
item.description: Public lecture at Tele2 Art Space, Yelagin Island, St. Petersburg. From fairy tale structure to Christian theology: five layers of meaning in Rowling's novels.

item.title: Benedict Spinoza: Heretic, Lens Grinder, and God as Substance
item.description: On the life and philosophy of Spinoza: excommunication from the synagogue, pantheism, the Ethics, and why Einstein invoked his name when asked about God.

item.title: Intelligent Design Is Not Science: The Kitzmiller v. Dover Case
item.description: A close reading of one of the most significant court cases in American educational history — Kitzmiller v. Dover Area School District (2005). Science, creationism, and the First Amendment.

item.title: Football as Quasi-Religion: A Scientific Analysis
item.description: Why Messi is called God, what football and religion have in common, and whether football is actually a religion. An analysis from the perspective of religious studies.

item.title: The Main Myth About Religion: Debunking Primordial Monotheism
item.description: What primordial monotheism is, where the idea came from, why it appeals to people, and why ethnographic data refutes it.

item.title: Godless: A Brief History of Atheism from Antiquity to the Present
item.description: A survey lecture on the history of atheism and freethought: from ancient impiety to the New Atheists of the twenty-first century.

item.title: The Religiosity of Young People Today: Data and Interpretations
item.description: A paper presented at the XXX International Educational Readings. What sociological data tell us about the religiosity of young people in Russia and the United States — and how it differs from older generations.

item.title: On Religion, Atheism, and Science: Interview for the Trickster Channel
item.description: Interview for Alexander Bydantsev's channel. On religious studies as a science, the Brights movement, agnosticism, scientism, and the limits of the scientific method.

item.title: Agnosticism: Between Belief and Unbelief
item.description: What agnosticism actually is, how it differs from atheism and scepticism, and why Bertrand Russell called himself an agnostic among colleagues but an atheist for public audiences.

item.title: Erasmus of Rotterdam: The Man Who Defined His Age
item.description: The life and ideas of Erasmus of Rotterdam: from illegitimate son of a priest to the intellectual arbiter of Europe. A close reading of The Praise of Folly, the dispute with Luther on free will, and Soviet reception.

item.title: Friedrich Nietzsche and His Critique of Christianity
item.description: Second lecture in the series on atheism and freethought. Nietzsche as a literary figure rather than a scientist: will to power, ressentiment, The Antichrist, and why his critique of religion is not scholarship.

item.title: John Toland: The Forgotten Genius of the Enlightenment
item.description: The first lecture in a series on the history of atheism and freethought. John Toland (1669/1670–1722): biography, Christianity not Mysterious, Letters to Serena, and his place in the history of European thought.

item.title: How Many Atheists Are There — and How Do You Count Them
item.description: A breakdown of a scientific paper on the methodology of counting atheists in the United States. Why direct surveys give 3% and indirect methods yield up to 32%.
